baseline.visibleGeometry: Broad smooth central slope is flanked by irregular shallow drainage. A sharply bounded, roughly polygonal raised form lies at the lower right, with a fairly level top and steep edges. A faint diagonal track or break crosses the upper left.
baseline.alternatives: The polygonal form could be a modern tank, stockpile, quarry remnant or engineered platform. Drainage and small bumps may be natural erosion or vegetation-related surface noise.
baseline.supportLimits: Most of the form appears measured, with interpolated patches around its margins. Its sharp outline and flatness need source-return and present-day imagery checks.

candidates.nextCheck: Inspect original ground returns, cross-sections and recent imagery for a modern engineered object.

enriched.visibleGeometry: Broad rounded slope between irregular drainage lines, with scattered small knolls and a prominent angular exposed rock in the southeast. A diagonal narrow trace crosses the northwest.
enriched.alternatives: Rock outcrops, erosion channels, vegetation effects and a footpath or vehicle track account for the visible forms.
enriched.supportLimits: Patch has scattered interpolated cells, especially at rough edges. No coherent enclosure or platform is clear across terrain views.

baseline.visibleGeometry: Several narrow incisions converge near the centre and continue toward the lower edge. Low rounded terrain occupies both sides; the right side has irregular small bumps and short parallel marks. The strongest linear forms follow the drainage network.
baseline.alternatives: Natural runoff erosion, tracks or field drainage could explain the lines; small bumps may reflect vegetation, stones or processing noise.
baseline.supportLimits: The central incision has substantial interpolated ground, especially near the convergence. Its apparent edges and depth are unreliable without original returns.

enriched.visibleGeometry: Several branching incised lines converge near the lower centre. A sloping rocky shoulder on the east bears small irregular knolls; western ground is smoother. Aerial vegetation follows the drainage.
enriched.alternatives: Seasonal drainage and erosion, exposed bedrock, stock trails, and vegetation or ground-classification gaps explain these traces.
enriched.supportLimits: The channel and rocky shoulder contain many interpolated cells. Their jagged edges should not be read as walls without original-return checks.

baseline.visibleGeometry: Dense, regularly spaced curved ridges cover the left field; finer nearly horizontal ridges cover the right. A strong north-south field edge separates them, and another straight edge crosses the lower right. A few isolated small rises lie in the right field.
baseline.alternatives: Cultivation or terracing, field boundaries and agricultural disturbance explain the regular spacing and alignment. Isolated rises may be rocks, spoil or vegetation artifacts.
baseline.supportLimits: Most field surfaces are measured. The north-south boundary and lower-right edge include interpolated cells, so small discontinuities there need source-return confirmation.

enriched.visibleGeometry: Regular closely spaced curved ridges cover the western field; parallel rows cover the eastern field. A nearly north-south boundary divides them, and an east-west track crosses the south.
enriched.alternatives: Ploughing or plantation furrows, field terraces and modern access or drainage boundaries match the aerial pattern and wider field network.
enriched.supportLimits: The north-south division has interpolated cells. Fine ridges are measured broadly, but their regular agricultural context limits interpretation.

references.name: Anta da Aldeia da Mata/ Tapadão 1/Couto dos Pucarinhos

baseline.visibleGeometry: Mostly smooth ground contains scattered small rounded rises. The most pronounced is near the upper left, with a narrow line extending south. A loose cluster of smaller bumps lies near the centre-right, and another pair near the lower centre. No continuous enclosure or broad platform is clear.
baseline.alternatives: Rocks, shrubs or tree-root mounds, spoil and modern ground disturbance could produce these rises. The narrow line could be a path or survey/processing artifact.
baseline.supportLimits: The bumps are mostly on measured model cells, but their sizes are small and individual return patterns are unverified. Image relief alone cannot establish whether they are constructed.

candidates.feature: Small isolated rise with adjacent linear mark
candidates.nextCheck: Inspect original ground returns and current aerial imagery for rock, vegetation or recent disturbance.

enriched.visibleGeometry: Mostly smooth open ground crossed by a narrow north-south track. Several small, irregular raised spots lie beside it, notably a cluster near the centre-right and isolated bumps toward the northwest and south.
enriched.alternatives: Exposed boulders or bedrock, small shrubs, and track-related disturbance fit the aerial patches and surrounding rocky terrain.
enriched.supportLimits: Ground is predominantly measured, but the bumps lack a coherent boundary or level surface. Imagery and model dates differ.

references.name: Anta da Aldeia da Mata/ Tapadão 1/Couto dos Pucarinhos

baseline.visibleGeometry: Several irregular knobby highs occupy the upper half, including a compact cluster near the upper right. A faint curved line follows the far right edge; the lower half is comparatively smooth.
baseline.alternatives: The knobs resemble exposed bedrock or scattered boulders. The curved line could be a track or field edge. Patchy interpolation around the highs can sharpen their apparent outlines.
baseline.supportLimits: The prominent high cluster contains many interpolated cells, so its internal shape is uncertain. Hillshade and local relief describe the same terrain model, not independent observations.

candidates.nextCheck: Inspect original ground returns and wider context to distinguish bedrock from any arranged structure.

enriched.visibleGeometry: Several isolated and clustered angular high spots occupy open ground. The largest cluster lies right of centre; a curved track crosses the lower half. Context shows similar outcrops across the surrounding pasture and a pond to the west.
enriched.alternatives: Exposed bedrock and loose boulders explain the irregular edges and their aerial appearance. The curved lines are visible tracks.
enriched.supportLimits: Some crest cells are interpolated, so fine outlines are uncertain. The class overlay adds no coherent structure evidence.

baseline.visibleGeometry: A narrow, branching north–south incision crosses the patch, with uneven sides and a dark gap near its lower end. Broad rounded slopes descend toward it from both sides. A faint east–west break joins it near mid-height.
baseline.alternatives: Likely a drainage or erosion channel, possibly modified by a path, ditch or field boundary. Angular texture along its margins may be model interpolation rather than built edges.
baseline.supportLimits: Much of the channel follows amber interpolated cells, and the lower dark gap is missing data. Its cross-section and small edge details need original returns.

enriched.visibleGeometry: A narrow branching channel runs north to south through the patch. Rounded slopes flank it, with short parallel lines on the eastern slope and scattered small bumps. Aerial imagery shows a vegetated drainage strip; context shows it continuing far beyond the patch.
enriched.alternatives: Natural erosion, a stream course and land-management terracing explain the lines and flanking slopes. Isolated bumps may be rocks or vegetation-related ground artifacts.
enriched.supportLimits: The channel has substantial interpolation and a dark missing patch near its southern end. Its jagged fine structure is unreliable. No independent class pattern defines a structure.

references.name: Anta da Aldeia da Mata/ Tapadão 1/Couto dos Pucarinhos

baseline.visibleGeometry: The central area is smooth, with broad shallow undulations and a faint branching low trending toward the lower left. Small isolated bumps lie near the upper edge and a rougher patch enters at the bottom. No coherent enclosure or platform is apparent.
baseline.alternatives: Shallow natural swales, minor rock or vegetation effects, and a change in surface roughness could explain the marks. The upper bumps may be rocks or residual surface objects.
baseline.supportLimits: Most central cells are measured, but the small edge highs include some interpolated cells. Subtle relief is near the visual scale of the model derivatives.

enriched.visibleGeometry: Mostly smooth open ground with a broad low rise in the lower centre, a few small rocky bumps along the top edge, and a faint diagonal track. The rise lacks a crisp perimeter or level summit.
enriched.alternatives: A natural undulation or bedrock swell fits the broad rise; the line is consistent with a field track and is visible in the aerial photograph.
enriched.supportLimits: Ground support is predominantly measured. The relief is weak and does not form an enclosed or angular feature; sparse fine bumps offer little independent evidence.

baseline.visibleGeometry: An irregular, roughly east–west break crosses the lower middle, separating rough upper ground from smoother sloping ground below. A narrow spur projects southward near the centre; several faint diagonal swales feed toward the break.
baseline.alternatives: The break may be a natural slope edge or drainage margin, with local erosion and rock exposure. A field edge is also possible. Its jagged appearance partly follows interpolated terrain cells.
baseline.supportLimits: Amber interpolation is concentrated along the break and around several small upper highs. The precise edge profile cannot be trusted without checking original returns and broader topography.

candidates.nextCheck: Examine original ground returns and wider context for a continuous constructed bank versus a natural slope or drainage edge.

enriched.visibleGeometry: A sinuous east-west bank crosses the lower middle, separating rougher northern ground from smoother southern pasture. Small scattered bumps occur north of it; the boundary continues outside the patch. Aerial imagery places a dirt track along the bank.
enriched.alternatives: A field boundary and track, with natural slope change and scattered trees or rocks, explain the visible pattern. It lacks an enclosed or discrete arrangement.
enriched.supportLimits: Most ground is measured, but interpolation clusters along the bank and at trees. Its exact edge shape is less certain; the aerial track supplies a direct modern explanation.

references.name: Anta da Aldeia da Mata/ Tapadão 1/Couto dos Pucarinhos

baseline.visibleGeometry: A compact cluster of angular high spots and short straight edges occupies the northwest quadrant, with one detached small knob south of it. A faint curving track passes just east. Another low rise sits farther south. The sharp cluster is consistent across illumination directions.
baseline.alternatives: Exposed bedrock, rubble, recent clearance or dumped material near a track; some sharp edges and gaps may reflect ground classification around objects.
baseline.supportLimits: The angular cluster contains many interpolated cells, so its internal edges cannot be trusted as measured ground. The surrounding terrain is mostly supported.

candidates.nextCheck: Inspect original ground returns, imagery and nearby mapped features to separate rock, recent rubble and built geometry.

enriched.visibleGeometry: An irregular cluster of sharp, angular raised forms lies west of a curving track, with a few detached bumps nearby. The cluster coincides with exposed grey rock in the photograph. Similar outcrops occur around the context area.
enriched.alternatives: Natural bedrock, boulders and erosion explain the irregular edges and repeated nearby forms; the linear trace is a present track.
enriched.supportLimits: The model is mostly measured, with interpolated pockets inside the rough cluster. Fine edges there need original-return checks. Photographs and terrain have different dates.

baseline.visibleGeometry: A broad sinuous slope break runs west to east across the upper half, separating rougher northern ground from a smoother southern surface. Small isolated hummocks occur on both sides. No coherent enclosure or platform is apparent.
baseline.alternatives: Natural slope or drainage edge, vegetation-related ground-model noise, erosion and field alteration; many northern speckles coincide with interpolation.
baseline.supportLimits: Interpolation is dense along the break and around several hummocks. The broad form is visible, but fine outlines are uncertain.

enriched.visibleGeometry: A curving break between rougher northern ground and a smoother southern slope crosses the patch. A narrow track follows part of this break. Small irregular bumps and shallow channels occur among trees to the north; scattered bumps also lie south. No coherent closed or rectilinear form is clear.
enriched.alternatives: Natural slope transition, drainage, bedrock and tree-associated ground disturbance; the photograph shows a track along the break.
enriched.supportLimits: Many small patches around trees and rough ground are interpolated. The break is mostly measured but its fine texture is uncertain; derivative layers reflect the same terrain model.

baseline.visibleGeometry: Regular parallel cultivation bands fill the western and southern fields. A straight north-south boundary meets an east-west linear bank or ditch near the centre. A second east-west field edge crosses the northeast. The intersection has a small raised irregularity.
baseline.alternatives: Field boundaries, track drainage and agricultural terracing explain the straight lines and repeated bands. The small junction rise may be a gate, vegetation or model interpolation.
baseline.supportLimits: Most field surfaces are measured, but the boundaries and junction have narrow interpolated strips. Their fine cross-sections need source-return checks.

enriched.visibleGeometry: Dense, evenly spaced curved ridges fill the western field; other parallel ridges occupy the upper and lower fields. Straight parcel boundaries meet a broad east-west track near the middle, with a small sharp bump at the junction. The photograph shows cultivated parcels and tree rows aligned with these traces.
enriched.alternatives: Agricultural furrows, field banks, track grading, fence or tree-line disturbance explain the repeated ridges and junction bump.
enriched.supportLimits: Most field surfaces are measured. Narrow boundary and vegetation strips contain interpolation, so their smallest apparent edges are less secure. The aerial image reflects a later season.

baseline.visibleGeometry: A long straight east-west depression or bank crosses the lower half, and a parallel field edge crosses the upper quarter. Repeated cultivation lines extend beyond them. A small isolated mound appears near the upper edge at roughly x310, y98.
baseline.alternatives: Agricultural boundaries, drainage, track grading and vegetation or stone piles are plausible. The small mound may be an isolated rock or agricultural debris.
baseline.supportLimits: The linear edges coincide with interpolated strips; the small mound is surrounded by measured terrain but its crest requires raw returns. No bounded arrangement is evident.

enriched.visibleGeometry: Two roughly east-west boundaries frame a broad, textured strip with scattered low bumps. Regular parallel cultivation ridges lie above and below. One compact raised knob sits near the upper boundary at about [310,100], where the photograph shows exposed rock beside a track.
enriched.alternatives: Field banks, track edges, cultivation, trees and natural rocks explain the visible forms. The knob has a direct exposed-rock counterpart.
enriched.supportLimits: The broad surfaces are mostly measured, but the boundary strips and scattered patches include interpolation. Their fine texture should not be treated as separate evidence from the model derivatives.
